headline: Use {arm:brisk-s.few}. It is the cheapest configuration that clears the overall gate, every cell floor and the latency budget.
lede: It reaches {measure.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.mean|pct} balanced accuracy with a p-ninety-five latency of {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.few.p95|int} ms. If complex news turns improved for {arm:nano-xs.few}, the far cheaper model would win.

slots.text: **{arm:brisk-s.few}**: balanced accuracy {measure.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.mean|pct}, p-ninety-five {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.few.p95|int} ms, and a fraction of the cost of any Atlas-M configuration.

**{arm:nano-xs.few}** is cheaper and clears the overall gate, but falls below the floor on complex news. **{arm:atlas-m.rubric}** is the most accurate at {measure.balanced_accuracy.atlas-m.rubric.mean|pct} but far too slow. **{arm:nano-xs.zero}** is the cheapest and misses the overall gate.
Complex news is the pick's weakest cell, the closest of its margins to the cell floor. Its errors are mostly medium turns labeled complex and the reverse; domain errors are rare.
Collect more complex news turns and re-test {arm:nano-xs.few} on that cell: if it clears the floor, it takes the recommendation at a fraction of the cost.

method.text: User turns from August and September, each labeled by two annotators, with disagreements adjudicated.
A turn is correct only if both complexity and domain match. Balanced accuracy weights the nine cells equally; traffic-weighted accuracy follows production traffic.
Binomial intervals per cell; the smallest cells have the widest.
Measured tokens times list price per million turns, at {meta.volume_per_month|int} turns a month.

sections.headline: Few-shot examples lift the small models most; rubric reasoning pays off only on the larger ones
sections.takeaway: Balanced accuracy for each model and prompt. It weights the nine target cells equally, so the largest segment cannot hide a weak cell.

sections.headline: Complex news is the hardest cell for every configuration, and the one that rules out Nano-XS
sections.takeaway: Accuracy per cell; rows are complexity, columns are domain.

sections.headline: Almost every complexity error is off by one step
sections.takeaway: Rows are the true label; each row sums to the whole. Simple turns are almost never called complex.

explore.title: Compare any two configurations, or change the gates
explore.recomputes: Which configurations pass every gate and the cheapest of them; a lower cell floor lets {arm:nano-xs.few} take the recommendation.

durable_claims.text: For a complexity-by-domain router, complex news is the cell that decides between models; {arm:brisk-s.few} clears it with few-shot examples.
